evidence: app/package.json:6-10 — no test script, empty devDependencies; zero test files anywhere in app/ (confirmed by find/ls and the measured facts: tests.files 0)
app/app/utils/poke.ts:17-56 — pure, high-risk helpers (humanize, idFromUrl, dexNumber, latestEnglishFlavorText, collapseWhitespace) have no unit tests despite being trivially testable
app/app/pages/index.vue:60-96 — filtering, pagination and URL-query building (buildQuery, page clamping, page reset on filter change) untested in app/
app/app/components/MovesTable.vue:38-58 — sort comparator with the subtle 'missing values sort last in both directions' rule is untested
coverage_of_risk.rationale: The agent wrote no tests at all. The app's densest transformation logic (name humanization, dex padding, species→card mapping, sort semantics, URL state) has no coverage except the external acceptance suite.

evidence: app/ — no test files exist (tests.files: 0), so there are no behavioural assertions either
behaviour_not_implementation.rationale: Nothing to evaluate; the criterion's floor ('no tests') applies.

evidence: app/app/utils/poke.ts:80-89 — fetchRecord converts every non-404 API error into null (rendered as 'Not found'); no test would catch a regression where a 500 no longer surfaces
app/app/utils/poke.ts:62-70 — promise cache eviction on failure and cache-key semantics are completely unguarded against refactor
app/app/pages/index.vue:38-45 — buildQuery default-omission rules (drop empty q/type/generation, drop page 1) would silently break under a data-layer refactor with nothing failing
regression_power.rationale: With no tests in app/, any refactor of the data layer or query-state logic passes silently. Once the acceptance suite is retired, behaviour changes ship undetected.

evidence: app/ — zero test files means zero noise, but also zero signal
signal_to_noise.rationale: No low-value tests exist, but only because no tests exist at all. Neutral per the rubric's 'no tests: 3'.

findings.issue: No test script, no devDependencies (@nuxt/test-utils, vitest), no test files — the app has no safety net beyond the harness-owned acceptance suite.
findings.suggestion: Add `@nuxt/test-utils` v4 + vitest (Nuxt's current recommended stack), a `test` script, and unit tests for the pure helpers in app/app/utils/poke.ts (humanize, idFromUrl, dexNumber, latestEnglishFlavorText, collapseWhitespace, cardsFromPokemonRefs) — all pure functions, cheap to test, high payoff.

findings.issue: cardsFromPokemonRefs (alternate-form exclusion, dedup by id, dex-number ordering, hidden-flag matching) is the app's most reused transformation and is untested; a refactor could silently reorder lists or drop/keep Mega forms.
findings.suggestion: Unit-test with fixture refs covering id>=10000 forms, duplicates (e.g. deoxys-normal + deoxys in a move's learned_by list), and hidden flag propagation.

findings.issue: URL-state logic (buildQuery default omission, page clamp via Math.min, page reset on filter change, 250ms debounce) is only partially covered by acceptance tests; edge inputs like page=0, page=999, page=abc, q with special characters are untested.
findings.suggestion: Add component tests (mountSuspended) asserting the URL produced for: filter change while on page 3, page param beyond totalPages, and non-numeric page.

findings.issue: The sortable-table comparator encodes the spec's 'missing values sort last in both directions' rule and the numeric-vs-string branch — exactly the kind of logic that breaks invisibly when someone 'simplifies' it.
findings.suggestion: Unit-test sortedRows (or the toggle/sort via mountSuspended) with rows containing null power/accuracy in both directions, and assert aria-sort state per column.

findings.issue: Method-table ordering (Level Up, Machine, Egg, Tutor, then others alphabetically) and default row ordering (level-up by level then name, others by name) are untested in app/; acceptance only checks one Pokémon's tables.
findings.suggestion: Unit-test the byMethod→ordered→rows pipeline (extract it to utils for testability) with a fixture containing an unknown custom method and mixed levels.

findings.issue: Version-group selection (games derived from pokemon.moves, ordered by version-group `order`, default = highest order, ?game= validation falling back to default) is untested; a regression could select the wrong default game or accept bogus query values.
findings.suggestion: Unit-test the game-list derivation and the selectedGame fallback: valid param, invalid param, Pokémon with no moves (empty list).

findings.issue: fetchRecord swallows every error type and returns null, so a transient 500 in the API renders a 404 'Not found' page with no test able to catch the conflation.
findings.suggestion: Test that non-404 failures are distinguishable (throw or return an error sentinel) rather than null; also cover the cache-eviction path at poke.ts:65-69.

findings.issue: getTypeIndex builds per-Pokémon type slots from 18 type records with slot-dedup and ordering — untested; a slot-order or dedup bug would scramble type badges on home cards and break the type filter.
findings.suggestion: Unit-test with fixture type records including a dual-slot Pokémon and an excluded type (stellar/unknown/shadow) referencing entries.

findings.issue: The hidden-ability flag is matched by exact URL comparison (entries.find(e => e.pokemon.url === ref.url)); if ref URLs ever differ in trailing-slash form the flag silently drops to false, and nothing tests it.
findings.suggestion: Unit-test the hidden predicate with fixture entries, or match by idFromUrl instead of string equality.

findings.issue: SSR 404 status is set only when useRequestEvent() exists and data is null; client-side navigation and the cached-promise path are untested for the not-found flow.
findings.suggestion: Add a test that a missing resource (e.g. /pokemon/missingno) renders NotFound and, on first load, returns HTTP 404.

summary: The app ships with zero tests of its own: no test script, no devDependencies, and no spec files, so every score except signal-to-noise bottoms out. The untested surface is exactly where regressions hurt: the humanize/dex/flavor-text helpers, cardsFromPokemonRefs, home-page URL-state and pagination, and the MovesTable sort comparator. The current Nuxt-recommended stack (@nuxt/test-utils v4 + vitest) would cover most of this cheaply since the risky logic sits in pure functions in app/app/utils/poke.ts.
